title: Water Sitting in the Belly of Our Older SOLANOs — Request for a Permanent Fix
abstract: Operator request for a permanent design answer to water collecting in the lower fuselage aft of the wing on early-build SOLANO aircraft, which is producing repeat corrosion findings and unplanned structural work at every heavy check.

sections.request: Every time one of our older SOLANOs goes into a heavy check we find the same thing under the aft cargo floor: standing water, soaked insulation and corrosion on the bottom of the frames where they meet the skin. On the last two aircraft the shop had to cut out and replace metal, which each time added between nine and fourteen days to a check that was planned for twenty-eight. We are now budgeting for the extra work as if it were certain, which tells you how routine it has become. Our people clean and re-treat the area at every opportunity but it comes back. What we would like is a design answer rather than another cleaning task — something that stops the water reaching the structure in the first place, or protects the structure properly when it does. It has to be something we can do inside a scheduled heavy check, because taking an aircraft out for this alone is not something we can absorb.
sections.background: We first raised this with your field service representative in 2023 after a check in Vienna ran long. Since then we have found the same condition on six of our nine pre-2005 aircraft. Our maintenance provider tells us the drainage in that part of the aircraft was designed for a drier cabin than the one our long-haul configuration actually produces, and that the galley and lavatory area above it leaks more than it should as the seals age. We have already fitted the drain valve improvement that was recommended to us in 2021 and it has not changed the picture. We are carrying an average of 2.6 unscheduled structural repairs per aircraft per heavy check against a fleet target of 0.5.
sections.expected_outcome: A modification that removes the recurring corrosion finding in this area for the remaining life of the aircraft, embodiable during a normal heavy check with the cargo compartment already open, and with a clear statement of what it does to our existing repeat inspection tasks so that we can take them out of our programme.

type_data.business_justification: Unplanned structural work in this area added an estimated 71 aircraft-days across six heavy checks in three years, at a direct shop cost the operator puts at 1.9 MEUR before the cost of lost availability.
